title: SwarmLeak: Does Coordination Improve Privacy Attacks on LLM Agents?
abstract: arXiv:2611.31791v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: LLM agents increasingly collaborate in group chats while holding tool access to confidential records, which makes the shared chat an attack surface. It remains unclear whether several colluding attackers extract such information more effectively than one. We introduce SwarmLeak, a red-teaming dataset of 24 synthetic group-chat scenarios across healthcare, law, finance, and software engineering, where attackers pose as colleagues to make a victim agent post protected fields despite an explicit confidentiality policy. With GLM 5.2 attacking five victim models through seven conversational strategies, we compare one attacker with a swarm of four sharing a private channel, matching scenarios, strategies, and a 200,000-token budget that also covers swarm coordination. Swarms show no advantage: a single attacker matches or exceeds them on every victim, and the share of runs leaking any field differs between conditions by at most 14.3 percenta

translated_title: SwarmLeak：协调能否提升对LLM智能体的隐私攻击效果？
translated_abstract: LLM智能体日益在群聊中协作，同时拥有访问机密记录的工具权限，这使得共享聊天成为一个攻击面。目前尚不清楚多个串通的攻击者是否比单个攻击者更有效地提取此类信息。我们提出了SwarmLeak，这是一个包含24个合成群聊场景的红队测试数据集，涵盖医疗、法律、金融和软件工程领域，攻击者在其中伪装成同事，诱使受害智能体在明确的保密政策下发布受保护的字段。通过使用GLM 5.2以七种对话策略攻击五个受害模型，我们比较了单个攻击者与共享私密通道的四体蜂群，两者在场景、策略以及20万token预算（该预算也涵盖蜂群协调开销）上保持一致。实验表明蜂群没有任何优势：单个攻击者在所有受害模型上都达到或超过蜂群的表现，两种条件下泄露任何字段的运行占比差异最多仅为14.3%。
tldr: 提出了SwarmLeak红队测试数据集，并通过实验证明多个攻击者协作的蜂群攻击在从LLM智能体群聊中提取机密信息方面并不比单个攻击者更有效。
en_tdlr: SwarmLeak, a red-teaming dataset of 24 synthetic group-chat scenarios, demonstrates that swarms of colluding attackers offer no advantage over a single attacker when extracting confidential information from LLM agents.
